title: GeoAI Klasyfikator: object-based land cover classification of drone and satellite imagery
description:
GeoAI Klasyfikator is open source software for supervised, object-based land cover mapping (GEOBIA) from RGB imagery: drone orthomosaics, aerial photographs and RGB composites of Sentinel-2 scenes, optionally supported by a digital surface model. It is distributed in three versions that share one computational core: a QGIS plugin, a command line program and a desktop application for Windows.

The processing chain consists of SLIC segmentation in CIELAB space, 19 object features computed from RGB (colour, visible-band vegetation indices ExG, VARI and NGRDI, GLCM texture, shape and neighbourhood context) or 24 with a surface model (including height above ground), a check of class separability before training (cross-validated Jeffries-Matusita distance), classification with Random Forest, and design-based accuracy assessment: stratified sampling of check points outside training objects, error matrix, user's and producer's accuracy, and area-weighted estimates of accuracy and class areas with 95% confidence intervals following Olofsson et al. (2014) and Stehman (2014). Optional pixel-level greenness refinement and a minimum mapping unit are available. The command line program and the Windows application batch-classify whole folders of images with one trained model, without mosaicking, and write a summary report of class areas per image. Fixed random seeds make results repeatable.

The user interface and documentation are in Polish. The archive contains the full source code, the user manual, the technical documentation for scientific use and the description of the method with all constants used in the code.

Polski opis. GeoAI Klasyfikator to otwarte oprogramowanie do nadzorowanej, obiektowej klasyfikacji pokrycia terenu ze zdjęć RGB z drona, zdjęć lotniczych i kompozycji RGB scen Sentinel-2, w trzech wersjach na jednym silniku: wtyczka QGIS, program wiersza poleceń i program okienkowy dla Windows. Łączy segmentację SLIC, 19 albo 24 cechy obiektów, ocenę rozróżnialności klas, klasyfikację metodą Random Forest i ocenę dokładności z estymacją powierzchni klas i przedziałami ufności 95%.
